newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P GIVES A LONG-TERM RATING TO NZS CONTACT ENERGY.
newsitem.headline: S&P GIVES A LONG-TERM RATING TO NZS CONTACT ENERGY.

text.p: Credit ratings agency Standard and Poor's on Thursday assigned its 'A' long-term and "A-1' short term credit ratings to New Zealand's Contact Energy Ltd.
It said the ratings outlook for Contact was stable.

S&P said the ratings reflected Contact's position as the second largest generator in New Zealand, its ownership of a diversified generating plant portfolio, strategic gas rights, good plant operations and a robust financial profile.
State-owned Contact was established in 1996, with 22 percent and 28 percent of New Zealand's wholesale electricity production and installed generator capacity respectively.

S&P said Contact had a well diversified asset portfolio. It noted that in a country where natural gas was a scarce resource, Contact also had the rights to 42 percent of the Maui gas field off the coast of the North Island.

"The field accounts for approximately 73 percent of the country's gas supply and provides Contact with a strategic resource for its own generation as well as a revenue stream going forward," S&P said.
It noted the government had announced more competition was needed in the electricity sector, but said Contact was well positioned to face that.
